terminal.description: A terminal in your workspace. `node ask.js server.js` starts your server, sends it each request in `requests.txt`, a body in three pieces, shows every answer and what the server printed, then stops it.

tasks.title: Read the whole body and keep the reading
tasks.description:
A volunteer's phone sends a reading as JSON in the body of `POST /readings`:

```json
{"tap":"north","litres":26}
```

Change `server.js` so that it reads the whole body, which may arrive in several pieces, turns it into a value with `JSON.parse`, and keeps the reading while the server runs. It answers with status `201`, the header `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`, and the reading it kept, as JSON: only its `tap` and its `litres`, whatever else was sent.

```json
{"tap":"north","litres":26}
```

Check sends readings of its own, each body in pieces, and sends the next piece only once your server has the one before.
nextSteps: Write a function that reads every piece of the request's body and gives back the whole of it as text.
In `POST /readings`, await it and turn the text into a value with `JSON.parse`.
Keep the reading, outside the function that answers, so it lasts from one request to the next.
Answer 201 with the reading, turned back into JSON text, and say it is JSON.
hints: The body is not on `req` when your function starts: it is still arriving. `req` is a stream, like a file read a line at a time, and it gives the body piece by piece.

`for await (const chunk of req)` gives each piece as a Buffer, and ends when the body does. `Buffer.concat(chunks).toString('utf8')` joins them into text. `JSON.stringify(value)` turns a value back into JSON text.
`const chunks = []; for await (const chunk of req) chunks.push(chunk); const reading = JSON.parse(Buffer.concat(chunks).toString('utf8'))`.

tasks.title: Answer the totals as JSON
tasks.description:
Imran wants to see how much each tap has used. Change `server.js` so that `GET /readings` answers with status `200`, the header `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`, and an object of each tap's litres added up, from every reading kept since the server started:

```json
{"north":38,"south":4}
```

Before any reading, it answers `{}`.

Check asks for the totals, sends readings of its own, and asks again.
nextSteps: Send two readings for the same tap and one for another, then `GET /readings`, all in `requests.txt`.
Add each kept reading's litres to its tap's total, or work the totals out from the readings when asked.
Answer with the totals turned into JSON text, and say it is JSON.
hints: `res.end` sends text, never an object: an object has to become JSON text first.
`JSON.stringify` turns a plain object into JSON, but a `Map` into `{}`. `Object.fromEntries(map)` makes a plain object of a Map.
`res.end(JSON.stringify(Object.fromEntries(totals)))`, after the status and the header.

tasks.title: Refuse a body that is not a reading
tasks.description:
Phones lose signal halfway, and people type. Change `server.js` so that `POST /readings` refuses a body it cannot use, with status `400`, a JSON body and the JSON header, keeps nothing, and goes on answering the next request:

- A body that is not JSON at all, such as half a reading or an empty body, gets `{"error":"The body is not JSON."}`.
- JSON that is not a reading gets `{"error":"A reading needs a tap and its litres."}`. A reading is an object whose `tap` is text that is not empty, and whose `litres` is a number, not text, of 0 or more.

Check sends a good reading, then bodies like these, then asks for the totals.
nextSteps: Add a line with half a reading to `requests.txt`, and a request after it, and see what happens to the server now.
Catch the error `JSON.parse` throws, and answer 400.
Then check what it gave back before you keep it.
Ask for the totals and make sure a refused body changed nothing.
hints: `JSON.parse` throws a SyntaxError on text that is not JSON, and an error nobody catches stops the whole server, not just one request.
`JSON.parse('null')` and `JSON.parse('"12"')` work: JSON can be any value, not only an object. `typeof value.litres === 'number'` is false for `"12"`.
`let reading; try { reading = JSON.parse(text) } catch { /* answer 400 here */ return }`, then check `reading` with `typeof` before you keep it.

tasks.title: Refuse a body that is too large
tasks.description:
A reading is a few dozen bytes. A body of a million bytes is a mistake, or someone trying to fill the laptop's memory. Change `server.js` so that a body of more than 1024 bytes gets status `413`, the JSON header and `{"error":"The body is too large."}`, is not kept, and the server stops reading it as soon as it is over the limit. A body of exactly 1024 bytes is still fine.

A sender does not always say how long its body is, so count the bytes as the pieces arrive.

Check sends a long body in many pieces without saying its length, one that says it, and one of exactly 1024 bytes, then asks for the totals.
nextSteps: In the function that reads the body, add up the length of each piece as it comes.
As soon as the total is more than 1024, stop reading and say the body is too large.
In `POST /readings`, answer 413 for it, before anything is read as JSON.
hints: Joining every piece and checking at the end means reading all of it first: a body without end would never be refused.
A Buffer's `length` is its number of bytes. Leaving a `for await` loop early with `return` or `break` stops reading the stream.
Inside the loop: `size += chunk.length; if (size > 1024) return null`, and answer 413 when the body comes back `null`.
